<page>
 Fort Bend County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0020
 Sara Davis, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Sara Davis
Date:
January 28, 2025
Location:
Offices of Brown & Shaw Law Group
Examining attorney:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Debra Moody, Brown & Shaw Law Group
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not put my full name on this, but you already have it from the case file. I'll answer your questions.
Q: Fair enough. Can you describe how the collision happened?
A: I was driving through an intersection in Sugar Land, turning left across the oncoming lanes. The light had been green for my
direction, but I was waiting for a gap in traffic. A pickup coming toward me didn't slow down, and its front end caught the
driver's side of my car.
Q: Did you see the pickup before the impact?
A: Only for a second. I saw headlights and started to brake, and then everything happened very fast.
Q: What is the first thing you remember after the collision?
A: My head hit the side window and I was dazed. I couldn't tell which way was up for a few seconds. I remember the airbag
going off and a smell of burnt plastic. Then a bystander was asking me questions and I kept losing the thread of what I was
saying.
Q: When did you first seek medical care?
A: The same day. An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They did a scan and diagnosed a concussion. They told me to
rest in a dark room and avoid screens for a while.
Q: Who has treated you since then?
A: My primary care doctor, and I was referred to a neurologist. I also started physical therapy for my neck because it was stiff
and sore. I still see the neurologist every few weeks.
Q: How are you doing day to day?
A: Better than the first few weeks, but not back to normal. Bright lights bother me, and I get headaches by the afternoon if I've
been reading or on my phone. I had to take a leave from my job for a while because I couldn't concentrate through a full workday.
I've been wroking shorter shfits now.
Q: Have you had any trouble with activities you enjoyed before the accident?
A: Yes. I used to run three mornings a week and I stopped completely for a long time. I also used to cook for my family most
nights, and now my husband does most of it. I get tired quickly and I forget things, like appointments, unless I wrtie them down
on paper.
</page>
